correctness.rationale: For every class, the positive two-state exchange flow is exactly affine. Composing phases gives a signed single-class difference (p_B-p_A)(1-e^{-alpha lambda_A h})(1-e^{-beta lambda_B h}), with complete cancellation of the initial water fraction. The total difference is C F1-D F2. The derivative of log(F1/F2) is a sum of two strictly positive terms because z/(exp(zh)-1) decreases strictly with z>0; its endpoints are q0 and 1. This proves the complete all-h classification including equality boundaries. Algebraic inversion yields the sharp positive weight interval, and Taylor/large-h expansions give both root limits. The example has positive underlying k,r and its root bracket is certified by exact rational alternating exponential series in check.py; 36,020 seeded comparisons are supplementary, not infinite proof. The statement explicitly restricts the phase ratio, parameter inequalities and terminal-stock objective.

value.rationale: Measured particle-class settling variation and bidirectional bed–water exchange motivate heterogeneous conservative retention dynamics. A single-class phase-order preference cannot flip with duration, whereas the weighted mixture has one exact time-scale crossover precisely within an explicit composition range, independently of unknown initial bed storage. The phase-length ratio does not affect whether reversal is possible. This discriminates a meaningful failure of single-type or single-duration surrogates and supplies an exact comparison benchmark for richer ecological transport models. No extrapolation to field interventions, unmeasured regimes or pollutant export is claimed.
